note: Provenance for every asset wired into the bundle. An asset is wired only after its bytes are compared against the canonical source; the marks are used AS SUPPLIED, so a later edit to one of these files is a brand violation rather than a style choice. scripts/design-system/ds-audit.mjs recomputes each sha256 and fails on drift, which is what makes a silent recolor impossible to land. `mirrors` are copies of the same canonical bytes served from elsewhere in the repo; they are hashed against the same value, because a mark that is correct in the bundle and recolored in public/ is the exact failure this file exists to catch. `rejected` records artwork that was fetched from the canonical source and then deliberately NOT wired, with the reason and the hash of exactly what was refused, so the next person does not re-fetch it and adopt it without looking.

assets.season: FIRST Robotics Competition 2027 — BIOCORE presented by Haas
assets.finding: Fetched 2026-08-24 from the FIRST season brand downloads page and adopted AS SUPPLIED. The page currently publishes the 2026-2027 season set: FIRST CANOPY (the umbrella season), BIOGLOW (FLL), BIOBUZZ presented by RTX (FTC), and BIOCORE presented by Haas (FRC 2027). BIOCORE is the FRC season, which is this team's program, and it is the coming season rather than a prior one, so no substitution was needed. The file is the vertical, full-color, RGB PNG from the archive's `Digital RGB` folder, 1730x1230, 8-bit RGBA — copied out of the zip byte-for-byte, verified by hashing the archive member and the copy in the bundle to the same sha256. Renamed to season-lockup.png ONLY: the bytes are untouched, and the generic path is what makes replacing this one file the entire annual reskin. THIS IS FIRST ARTWORK AND THE FIRST USAGE RULES APPLY IN FULL — never recolored, rotated, skewed, cropped, bordered, or combined with added text. The slot renders it under object-fit: contain (tokens/image-slot.css), so SeasonLockup's 240x240 default letterboxes it to 240x171 rather than distorting or cropping it; the artwork carries its own filled plates over transparency, so one file serves squadron, field and paper and no reverse variant is required. NOTE FOR THE PAPER GROUND: the artwork contains a yellow element. It is FIRST's yellow, not Techmen Gold, and the no-gold-on-paper rule does not reach it — supplied artwork may not be recolored, so there is nothing to fix here and nobody should try. The /_ds gold-on-paper proof reads computed colour and cannot see inside an , so it will not report this either way.
assets.toResolve: Replace this one file each January when FIRST publishes the next FRC season logo, re-hash it here, and update the SeasonLockup name and years in the decks that use it. Nothing else changes.

hazards.found: npm run gen-icons wrote SOLID #005bff squares over public/pwa-192x192.png, public/pwa-512x512.png and public/apple-touch-icon.png. The icons on disk were mark artwork in #FFE629 and were NOT produced by that script, so running it destroyed three correct mark-derived icons and replaced them with flat blue. It was left runnable through the asset-swap pass, because rewriting it was a separate call.
hazards.done: The script was rewritten rather than deleted. It now rasterises public/assets/logos/Mark-Gold.svg through headless Chrome, and REFUSES TO RUN unless that file hashes to the sha256 recorded in this file — an icon generator that will happily rasterise a recolored mark is how a wrong gold reaches every home screen on the team at once. Its scales were set by measuring the ink bounding box of the shipped icons and matching them (51.6-52.2% of canvas against a shipped 52.0-52.2%; maskable 38.5% against 38.7%), and --check verifies the mark without writing while --out writes elsewhere to compare first. The shipped icons were left in place: they are correct and hand-tuned.
hazards.note: Kept rather than deleted so the reason the hash guard exists is still readable. The guard in gen-icons.js is downstream of this record: if the mark ever stops matching, the generator stops rather than propagating it.

hazards.found: The APP's --gold token was #D4AF37, a generic web metallic gold and not a team brand color, with --hr-regular / --hr-build carrying it too. After the mark swap the mark rendered canonical gold next to app chrome in the older gold, visible on the landing page where the mark and the SIGN IN button no longer matched. It was left alone through the asset-swap pass because changing it restyles every app surface.
hazards.done: --gold is now #FFE629 and the whole ramp is re-derived from it: --gold-bright #FFF06B, --gold-dim #C7B320, --gold-a08/a14/a24, --hr-regular and --hr-build. Two hardcoded rgba(212,175,55,.08) washes (MemberSkillsHome.css, ParentHomePage.css) were repointed at var(--gold-a08) so the token is again the only source. Because #FFE629 is brighter, the AREA was reduced rather than the saturation: the six large primary actions (.landing-cta, .gate-submit, .gate-signout, .login-card submit, .pr-submit, .ma-submit) became a gold label and gold border on the dark plate with the fill kept for hover and focus, and .gate-signout was then moved out of the gold family — steel border, ash label — because a sign-out is neither identity nor an active state. Its keyboard focus ring stays the app-wide gold one: a focus ring is the system indicating keyboard position rather than the control's identity, so a per-control ring color makes the indicator less reliable, and focus is an active state, which is what gold is for. Roughly sixty small gold fills (dots, chips, tabs, progress bars, per-row buttons) were left filled, because small-area gold IS the active state.
hazards.note: This bundle was NOT the thing that changed. Its tokens were already canonical and are scoped under .frc-deck precisely so the deck layer and the app layer cannot collide; the collision was entirely inside the app's own :root.

rejected.finding: RECOLOR CHECK FAILS. The canonical seal carries #ffe623 in all 71 of its gold declarations (41 stroke, 30 fill; the only other colour value anywhere in the file is fill="none"). The published Techmen Gold is #FFE629, which is what Mark-Gold.svg and Type-Gold.svg both carry, byte-for-byte, fetched from the same branding page in the same pass. #ffe623 is a near-gold: it differs only in the blue channel (0x23 = 35 against 0x29 = 41), which is precisely the class of drift this file exists to catch and is invisible to the eye at seal scale. The fetch was repeated from a cold request and both downloads hash identically, so this is the published artwork rather than a transfer fault. The file was NOT copied into assets/team/, ASSETS.seal stays null, and SealMark keeps rendering its marked empty slot.
rejected.consequence: DeckFooter defaults to mark="logotype", so wiring Type-Gold.svg clears the empty box on the footer rail of every sheet of every deck, which was the blocking symptom. The seal slot still renders empty in the places that ask for it in the sheet BODY - CoverSheet and ClosingSheet - and on a DeckFooter explicitly passed mark="seal".
rejected.toResolve: Ask the team either for a seal exported at #FFE629, or for an explicit ruling that #ffe623 is the intended seal value. Either answer is a small change: drop the file at assets/team/5669-Seal.svg, import it in assets.js beside the Type imports, set ASSETS.seal, and move this record out of `rejected` and into `assets` so ds:audit hash-pins it like the rest.
